sentences.text: Researchers used a rat Schwann cell line to investigate whether pyroptosis, a specific form of programmed cell death, contributes to nerve cell damage induced by the drug bortezomib.

Exposure to the drug lowered cell survival and increased damage markers in a dose-dependent manner, a process associated with the accumulation of reactive oxygen species and the activation of pyroptosis pathways.

Protein analysis revealed strong activation of caspase-1 and caspase-3 signaling pathways alongside increased inflammatory proteins, while blocking both pathways simultaneously provided greater protection than inhibiting either one alone.
Treatment with the antioxidants N-acetyl-l-cysteine and vitamin C reduced reactive oxygen species levels, suppressed the pyroptosis pathways, and lessened the observed cell injury.

The authors conclude that bortezomib triggers pyroptotic damage in Schwann cells through coordinated pathway activation dependent on reactive oxygen species, suggesting pyroptosis as a potential target for future therapeutic development.
